key_insight: UNICON is a foundation model that learns predictive relationships from numerical examples in context and transfers them across scientific and social domains, even to disciplines unseen during training.
engineering_relevance: It suggests a new general-purpose modeling approach for scientific forecasting and decision support when labeled data are sparse, heterogeneous, or out-of-domain.
method: Uses graph-based in-context examples from a system to infer the underlying predictive relation.
Applies the learned relation to new queries from the same system without retraining.
Combines with language-model agents to improve performance on unseen disciplines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that across multiple scientific and social systems, including unseen disciplines, UNICON approaches specialist performance without retraining and can surpass state-of-the-art specialists when paired with language-model agents.
watch_item: Generalization depends on the diversity of the training corpus, so performance may weaken on highly novel systems if the numerical context is too different from the training distribution.
paper_title: A foundation model of numerical intelligence with cross-disciplinary generalization
